title: Por vs. para
invitation: Want a quick lesson on why Spanish uses por or para here?
summary: Both words can correspond to English words such as “for,” but Spanish chooses between them according to the relationship being expressed. Learn the relationship, not an English one-word translation.

blocks.text: Instead of memorizing one English translation, notice what the phrase is doing: showing a path or reason, expressing a purpose or destination, naming a beneficiary, setting a deadline, and so on.
Use por for a path, route, or area something moves through or along.
Use por when the phrase gives a cause, reason, or motivation.
Por qué asks for a reason. Treat the whole interrogative expression as a unit rather than swapping por and para mechanically.
Constructions such as por eso and por lo que connect prior information to a consequence or result.
Use por for a means, method, route, channel, or medium in many common constructions.
Use por in many exchange, price, replacement, and substitution relationships.
Por appears in distributive patterns such as uno por uno: one by one.
Use para to point toward an intended purpose or goal. Para + infinitive is a common way to express what something is done in order to accomplish.
Use para to point toward a destination, endpoint, or goal.
Use para to identify an intended recipient or beneficiary in many common contexts.
Use para for many deadlines or target times.
Expressions such as por la mañana and por la noche use por to place an event in a time-of-day frame. Learn this as a common time expression, not as a por-versus-para guessing rule.
Por fin is a fixed expression meaning finally or at last. Treat the whole expression as one chunk.

RULE.es.por_para.por_path_route.summary: This is a path or area being moved through or searched through, so Spanish uses por.
tips: Think: through, along, around, or by way of.

RULE.es.por_para.por_cause_reason.summary: This phrase gives the cause or reason something happened, so Spanish uses por.
tips: If because of fits the meaning, por is a strong clue.

RULE.es.por_para.por_reason_question.summary: This is the fixed interrogative expression por qué, which asks for a reason.
tips: Treat por qué as a whole expression here.

RULE.es.por_para.por_consequence.summary: This construction connects what came before to a result or consequence.
tips: Treat expressions such as por eso or por lo que as units, not as an open por-or-para blank.

RULE.es.por_para.por_means_channel.summary: This phrase tells the means, method, route, channel, or medium by which something happens, so Spanish uses por.
tips: Ask: how or by what channel?

RULE.es.por_para.por_exchange_substituti.summary: This phrase expresses an exchange, price, replacement, or substitution, so Spanish uses por.
tips: Think: one thing in exchange for another.

RULE.es.por_para.por_distributive.summary: This is a distributive pattern, such as uno por uno: one by one.
tips: Treat the repeated-unit pattern as a chunk rather than a basic por-or-para choice.

RULE.es.por_para.para_purpose.summary: This phrase points toward what an action is intended to accomplish, so Spanish uses para.
tips: If in order to fits, para is a strong clue.

RULE.es.por_para.para_destination_goal.summary: This phrase points toward a destination, endpoint, or goal, so Spanish uses para.
tips: Picture an arrow aimed at the endpoint.

RULE.es.por_para.para_beneficiary.summary: This phrase identifies the intended recipient or beneficiary, so Spanish uses para.
tips: Ask: who is this intended for?

RULE.es.por_para.para_deadline.summary: This phrase treats a time as a deadline or target point, so Spanish uses para.
tips: Think of the date or time as an endpoint you are aiming toward.

RULE.es.por_para.por_time_frame.summary: This is a common time-of-day expression using por, such as por la mañana or por la noche.
tips: This is an extension pattern. Learn the phrase as a natural time expression rather than forcing it into the beginner cause/path rules.

RULE.es.por_para.por_fin_fixed.summary: Por fin is a fixed expression meaning finally or at last.
tips: The useful unit here is por fin as a whole chunk.
